observed: The old job becomes killed around the original five-second deadline. The second job is already registered before that and remains running until the new task independently reaches its 20-second deadline; its tool result then reports AbortError. The log does not establish where the PowerShell process was waiting.
hypothesis: Parallel non-interactive Windows PowerShell jobs share a module-analysis cache that is written asynchronously. Test the documented NUL cache opt-out in each managed shell process. The macOS PowerShell Core issue is only a related hypothesis, not proof of this Windows 5.1 failure.
